messages.content: Why do we only use 10% of our brains?

response.text:
The idea that humans only use 10% of their brains is actually a myth. This misconception has been debunked by neuroscientists. In reality, we use virtually every part of our brain, and most of the brain is active almost all the time. Brain imaging research has shown that even when we are at rest, our brains are still active, and different tasks and activities engage different parts of the brain.

The myth may have originated from misinterpretations or misrepresentations of neurological research in the early 20th century, or from the fact that at any given moment, only a small percentage of neurons may be firing. However, this does not mean that the rest of the brain is inactive or unused. Each part of the brain has a known function, and damage to even small areas can have significant effects on cognition and behavior, further indicating that we use all parts of our brain.
